subject: koala
pitch: A sleepy koala hugging a eucalyptus branch. Soft ash-grey fur with a cream chest and cream-lined fluffy ears, a big black leathery nose, half-closed drowsy brown eyes, strong grey paws with dark claws, and a sprig of blue-green eucalyptus leaves in one hand, mid-munch.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a three.js koala built from primitives sitting on a branch with leaves, roughly 0.75m tall with the ground at y=0. I'm sketching the main components starting with a grey ellipsoid body positioned around y≈0.35.

Now I'm detailing the chest as a cream ellipsoid, the head as a slightly flattened sphere up at y≈0.78, and the ears as layered grey/cream cylinders on either side. For the face, I'm working out a leathery black nose ellipsoid and half-closed eyes made from a brown eye sphere paired with a grey hemisphere eyelid cap using a partial sphere geometry to get that sleepy koala look.

Covering the full front would mean the eye looks closed, but I only want the upper half shaded for a half-closed look, so pole-forward orientation isn't quite right for partial coverage. Maybe a simpler approach works better: using a flattened box shape as the eyelid instead of a sphere cap.

I'm positioning the lid as a grey box offset above eye center so it covers roughly the top portion while leaving the lower half visible, which reads as a drowsy expression. Working out exact coordinates for eye placement relative to the head sphere so the eyes sit properly embedded at the front surface.

Now I'm placing the nose as a big black ellipsoid protruding from the lower head front, calculating surface position so it sits correctly. For the body I'm using a large ellipsoid resting at ground level, and thinking through how to position a branch beneath the koala so it looks like it's sitting in a tree while still touching the ground.

I'm deciding the branch should instead be something the koala hugs in its arms, like a eucalyptus limb — trying a diagonal cylinder shape that runs from the ground up near the koala's chest, leaning at an angle so the arms can wrap around it naturally.

I'll add a helper that builds a limb mesh between two points, orienting it via quaternion rotation from the Y axis to the direction vector, positioned at the midpoint. Then I'm placing the branch endpoints to lean across the koala's body at an appropriate height.

For foliage, I'm planning to scatter leaf shapes along the branch using flattened, scaled spheres as simple lanceolate eucalyptus leaves in blue-green tones, rather than a more complex custom shape geometry.

I'm positioning a eucalyptus sprig in the koala's paw near its mouth, with a short stem running from the paw up toward the mouth and leaves clustered at the tip so it looks mid-munch.

Rather than keeping the branch and sprig on the same side, I'm moving the branch to the opposite (-X) side, running diagonally from near the base up and outward. The free paw holds the sprig while the other arm wraps around to grip the branch, so I'm computing the branch's position at the arm's height to place that paw accurately on its surface.

Now I'm building out the rest of the body: haunches and paws as ellipsoids with small dark claw cones, and ears as flattened rounded discs positioned near the top sides of the head, angled outward and slightly forward.

I'm also considering adding a subtle fur texture — maybe a small seeded-noise canvas texture mapped onto the grey body material to give it a fuzzier look, keeping it lightweight and simple.

For the eucalyptus branch, I'm placing leaves along the branch using a brown bark material and green leaf material, scattering sphere-based leaf geometry at intervals with perpendicular offsets and varied orientation for a natural look.

Now I'm setting up a seeded random generator and defining the color palette for the fur, cream, black, eye, claw, and bark materials.

Adding fur texture generation...

Still writing limb geometry...

I'm making the limb function accept separate top and bottom radii for tapering, with the branch base thicker near the ground and narrowing upward, then moving on to defining the koala's right arm from shoulder to paw.

For the paw placement I'm checking the distance from the branch axis to ensure the paw sphere touches the branch surface rather than floating or overlapping too deeply, adjusting coordinates until the gap roughly matches the paw's radius minus the branch's radius at that height. I'm also confirming the shoulder point sits properly embedded within the body ellipsoid so the arm connects naturally to the torso.

Now I'm working out the right arm holding a eucalyptus sprig, placing the shoulder and paw coordinates, then running the stem from the paw up toward the mouth so it looks like the koala is nibbling on it near the front of the face. I'm checking the head ellipsoid's cross-section at the mouth height to make sure the sprig tip lines up just in front of the face surface, then positioning the paw sphere around the stem and starting to lay out leaf clusters along the stem's length from the paw end toward the tip.

Next I'm scattering individual leaves along the branch using randomized offsets and orientations so they look naturally eucalyptus-like, shaping each as a thin elongated ellipsoid and aligning it along a perpendicular-plus-upward direction vector. Then I'm moving on to the ears, setting up the outer cylindrical shape and a cream-colored inner disc that pokes out slightly to the side, and starting to add small tufts of fur around the ear edges for texture.

Now I'm placing the eyes on the front of the head as small brown spheres with eyelid boxes positioned just above and forward of them, and working out the tilt angles so the lids slant downward toward the nose to give the koala a sleepy, drowsy expression—figuring out the sign of the rotation based on which side of the face each eye is on.

I'm shaping the head as a broadened sphere to match a koala's wide face, adding a cream-colored chest ellipsoid embedded partway into the body, and considering a cream chin patch near the nose for the characteristic white muzzle coloring before moving on to the haunches.

Now I'm defining the haunches, feet, and toe placements as scaled ellipsoids, then adding small dark cone-shaped claws at the toe tips, rotated to point forward and angled slightly downward.

Ground disc isn't necessary. I'll add subtle fur texture to the body using a canvas-generated texture function.

Finishing the canvas texture setup and applying it to the fur material with repeat wrapping set to (2,2).

Now I'm naming this creature "Sleepy Koala" and starting the full implementation, including a seeded random number generator for procedural variation.

Building the root group and setting up the fur texture and material, falling back to a grey tone if no texture is generated. Now I'm defining the color palette, starting with the cream shade for the chest and ears.

Adding a helper function for attaching meshes to the root, plus a blob-creation utility that builds scaled sphere meshes positioned anywhere in space -- useful for sculpting the koala's rounded body parts.

I'm also writing a limb-building function that creates a cylinder stretching between two points, orienting it correctly using quaternion rotation so it connects naturally like a branch or leg.

Adding leaf placement loop...

Placing leaves at an offset from the branch with an outward-and-up orientation, using small flattened blobs rotated to face that direction...

Totaling 36 leaf meshes across the branch and sprig. The sprig adds its own stem with a dozen leaves scattered with randomized angles and slight size variation, then I'm moving on to shaping the left paw.

I'm placing the left paw blob near the stem base and the right paw further out with its own scale, deciding to skip claws on the right paw and instead save them for the feet. Then I'm laying out both arms as limbs connecting shoulders to paws, picking consistent radii for each.

Now I'm building the body: a main fur blob, a cream chest blob positioned to protrude slightly at the front, haunches on both sides, and a head blob with a cream chin underneath, checking that each piece's position and scale keeps proportions believable.

Then I'm placing the nose as a small black blob near the head's front, and eyes slightly above it, verifying each feature's protrusion from the head surface stays consistent.

Now sizing the eyelid box at depth 0.245 and checking coverage - it spans y 0.801–0.835 against the eye's 0.765–0.835 range, covering roughly the top half, which looks right, and its width of 0.085 comfortably spans the eye's 0.07 width too.

For the eye highlight, I'm adding a tiny white sphere positioned under the lid for a subtle glint. Then moving to the ears: computing where the head's curved surface sits at x=±0.15 (around y=0.91), placing cylinder-shaped ears rotated to lie along the X axis just above that point.

For the inner ear detail, I'm positioning a smaller cream-colored cylinder slightly offset from the outer ear piece, working out the overlap so it pokes out just enough to read as a fluffy rim. Realizing a plain cylinder doesn't quite match a koala's ear look, I'm reconsidering and planning to swap it for a torus shape instead to get a better fuzzy-ring effect.

Now I'm switching to a torus for the cream rim, oriented with its axis along X via a y-axis rotation, and adding eight small cream sphere "tufts" spaced around the rim's circumference to give it a fluffy texture. I'm checking that the ear position aligns properly with the head surface before moving on to blocking out the feet.

For the feet, I'm placing fur blobs and adding claws as small cones angled at each toe, working out the rotation math so the cone tips point forward and downward correctly from the paw.

I'm deciding to skip the mouth detail since the chin covers it, and skipping the tail too. For the branch, I'm adding a small twig extending outward from a point partway along the main branch.

Adding twig leaves...

I'm double-checking the function signature and making sure the root returns as a proper THREE.Object3D before finalizing the code.
